title: Invoker sandbox with progressive result attenuation and recursion sentinel
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Background:
The invocation/execution loop is the heart of our multi-tool orchestration. Customer incidents and internal fuzzing have surfaced two recurring problems: (1) unbounded recursive tool-invocation cycles when model directives indirectly re-trigger the same tool (or chain), and (2) noisy or large injected tool outputs that destabilize downstream streaming and structured-output parsing. Existing mitigations (simple depth counters and global timeouts) are coarse and sometimes either break legitimate long chains or allow pathological loops to consume significant runtime and telemetry budget.

Goal:
Build a sandboxed invoker layer that: (a) progressively attenuates or truncates injected tool results when heuristics indicate amplification risk, (b) enforces a recursion sentinel that can quarantines re-entrant chains with programmable policies per-route/model, and (c) emits fine-grained telemetry for root-cause analysis and automatic rollbacks. The solution should be pluggable into the current executor pipeline with minimal changes to caller-facing APIs and support per-customer and per-route overrides (for Dedicated/Private customers).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement a new global policy UI in Console (docs-only config knobs).
- Not replacing model-side safety classifiers; this is an execution-layer safety net.

Design proposals (high level):
1) Sandboxed Invoker Wrapper:
- Each external tool call is executed inside a lightweight sandbox object with metadata: invocation_id, chain_id, depth, origin_route, model_hint, token_cost_estimate.
- The sandbox enforces three resource guards: token budget, time budget, and recursion horizon. Budgets are computed from route SLO + model profile.
- Tool results are tagged with provenance and a score for amplification risk (see below).

2) Progressive Result Attenuation:
- Define an amplification heuristic that scores tool outputs by: size growth ratio w.r.t input, presence of repeating structural markers, emergence of new tool invocation patterns, and heuristic entropy (very low or very high entropy often indicates problematic outputs).
- Policy types: passthrough, attenuate-summary, truncate-edges, redact-sensitive, and stash-for-review. Default policy: attenuate-summary when amplification_score > threshold1; stash-for-review if > threshold2 and customer is enterprise with review enabled.
- Attenuation modes: generate an abstractive summary (size-limited), or produce a concise structured skeleton that preserves fields required by the caller (structured-output contracts). The attenuation operation uses a small, constrained runtime instruction (local model or deterministic summarizer) to avoid external tool restarts.

3) Recursion Sentinel and Quarantine:
- A chain-level sentinel tracks the set of invoked tool signatures (tool_id + signature_hash). If an invocation would re-enter a signature already seen in the chain, flag recurrence.
- Recurrence policy: (a) soft-sentinel: inject a synthetic token warning into model context (keeps chain but signals risk), (b) hard-sentinel: abort the invocation with a controllable fallback (use cached response or alternative tool).
- Quarantine: when aborting due to sentinel breach, persist the chain snapshot (KV cache excerpt, recent prompts, tool outputs) tagged for debugging and optionally surfaced to Console for enterprise customers with debug retention.

4) Route/Customer Overrides and Compatibility Layers:
- Expose per-route config: recursion_depth_limit, attenuation_thresholds, default_fallback_tool, and audit_mode. Defaults chosen conservatively to avoid breaking existing integrations.
- Compatibility: for older clients that depend on unconditional passthrough of tool results, support an \"exec_compat: true\" flag that uses only sentinel checks (no attenuation) but with stricter quotas and telemetry. Document compatibility trade-offs.

Telemetry and Observability:
- Emit structured events for: invocation_start, invocation_end, attenuation_applied (with type), sentinel_breach, quarantine_written. Include chain_id, origin_route, model_hint, amplification_score, and token_budget_used.
- Add new Console dashboard panels: \"Execution Amplification\" (distribution of amplification_score), \"Recursion Events\" (per-route frequency), and link from invocation traces to quarantined snapshots.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit + integration tests covering: benign long chains (no attenuation), controlled amplification (attenuation triggers), recurrence detection & policies, and compatibility flag behaviour.
- System tests that run a battery of fuzzed prompts and tools; measure false-positive attenuation rate < 3% on a curated corpus and detection rate > 95% for injected recurrence patterns from our incident corpus.
- End-to-end benchmark: median 95th percentile latency regression < 5% on standard streaming routes when attenuation is not applied; with attenuation applied, overall latency must remain within route SLOs for P99.
- Telemetry events emitted and visible in Console staging dashboards.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: library surface and sandbox abstraction; chain_id propagation changes in executor (ENG-430112-A).
- Week 2: amplification heuristic implementation and unit tests; initial attenuation strategies (deterministic summarizer) (ENG-430112-B).
- Week 3: sentinel detection, quarantine write path, and compatibility flag (ENG-430112-C).
- Week 4: integration tests, telemetry schema, and Console staging dashboard PR (console-2489).

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.exec_sandbox.enabled=false by default in Hosted. Enable in Canary for internal routes and 2 pilot customers on Dedicated. Ramp up after 1 week of stable telemetry.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Quarantine snapshots may contain PII. Use per-customer KMS encryption and ensure snapshots respect data residency toggles. Only expose snapshots to customers with audit_role.
- Ensure attenuation redaction mode removes known PII patterns (SSNs, API keys) before persistence.

Backwards compatibility trade-offs and docs:
- Document behaviour for exec_compat flag in API docs and migration guide: recommended migration path is to opt into attenuation in staging and monitor amplification dashboard.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Do we prefer a small local summarizer (deterministic, faster) vs. a model call for high-quality attenuation? Local summarizer reduces cost but may increase false positives. (PM leaning: start local, add model option behind flag.)
- What are safe amplification thresholds across different model families and sequence lengths? We will bootstrap with conservative defaults and refine from telemetry.
